documents.title: SHSU Generative AI Guidance
documents.summary: A university guidance page with separate sections for students, faculty and staff. It sets no AI rule itself and says it is up to each instructor to set the policy, tells students to ask and disclose, ties unauthorized use to the Academic Honesty Policy, and gives staff data-protection advice and approved tools.
documents.stance_why: The page says "While there is no defining university policy on AI" and "It is up to each instructor to specify an AI policy for that particular class." It sets no default of its own, so the stance is delegates.

units.why: The student guide says "It is up to each instructor to specify an AI policy for that particular class." This hands the rule to instructors, so it is P04 (per-instructor rule); it binds instructors, is a before-course design matter, and "up to" gives discretion (may).
units.anchor: It is up to each instructor to specify an AI policy for that particular class.

units.why: "You can ask your professors about AI use in your classes" tells students to ask instructors when unsure ("If you're not sure, ask!"), which is P10. Addressed to students, communicating expectations at course start; the surrounding advice makes it a should.
units.anchor: You can ask your professors about AI use in your classes
units.policy: Students who are not sure about AI use in a class ask their professors, and can ask IT@SAM or the library for other questions.

units.why: "reach out to IT@SAM or the library for other questions" points students to human support units, so P72 (human help alongside AI). Student-facing, general, and a suggestion ("can").
units.anchor: you can reach out to IT@SAM or the library for other questions
units.fit_note: Human help is offered for general AI questions, not as a substitute for AI use.

units.why: "It is important to learn how and when to use AI" frames learning to use AI as a skill students should acquire; closest to P44 (AI as a skill), but no professional or employer reference, so it is a partial fit. Principle statement, so informs.
units.anchor: It is important to learn how and when to use AI.
units.fit_note: States learning when and how to use AI is important, without any employer or professional-skill claim.

units.why: "SHSU has access to Microsoft’s Copilot, Gemini, and Google NotebookLM using your SHSU sign on" tells students the university provides sanctioned AI tools, so P17. It is a fact (informs) delivered to students, general phase.
units.anchor: Gemini, and Google NotebookLM using your SHSU sign on
units.policy: SHSU provides students access to Microsoft Copilot, Gemini and Google NotebookLM with their SHSU sign on.

units.why: "Using AI to complete work without permission may violate" the Academic Honesty Policy: unauthorized AI use is classed as misconduct, so P36. Addressed to students, when-misuse phase, a warning ("may violate") hence should-not.
units.anchor: Using AI to complete work without permission may violate

units.why: "Always check with your instructor or supervisor before you use it" is a directive to ask before using AI. P10 (ask first); it is a distinct instruction from the earlier "ask" advice, and "Always" makes it a strong should.
units.anchor: Always check with your instructor or supervisor before you use it.

units.why: "Any assignments that allow the use of AI tools should include an acknowledgement of your AI use" requires acknowledgement on permitted AI work: P24 (disclose with each submission). Student, during-work, "should" modality; stance permit because it assumes use is allowed with disclosure.
units.anchor: should include an acknowledgement of your AI use

units.why: "the simple use of generative AI is not necessarily an academic integrity problem" says use alone is not misconduct. No type states this (P36 is about misconduct, P02 about default permission), so UNCOVERED rather than a stretch.
units.anchor: the simple use of generative AI is not necessarily an academic integrity problem
units.uncovered_note: Using generative AI is not in itself an academic-integrity violation; whether it is misconduct depends on the instructor's boundaries.

units.why: "undisclosed use of generative AI in assignments outside the boundaries that an instructor has set ... may constitute a violation" of Academic Honesty: improper AI use is misconduct, so P36. P28 (nondisclosure as violation) was considered, but the violation hinges on going outside the instructor's boundaries as well as non-disclosure, so P36 fits better. Repeated verbatim in the student and faculty sections; coded once.
units.anchor: undisclosed use of generative AI in assignments outside the boundaries

units.why: "Instructors should make sure that students are informed of course expectations regarding how AI may or may not be used" tells instructors to communicate their AI rules, and whether to cite, which is P09. Instructor-addressed, course-start, "should".
units.anchor: Instructors should make sure that students are informed of course expectations

units.why: "these detection tools are recognized as deeply flawed" with false positives and negatives states detectors are unreliable, P39. A fact, so informs; unit_stance neutral. Appears twice, coded once.
units.anchor: these detection tools are recognized as deeply flawed

units.why: "Instructors should be cautious in relying on an AI detection tool to take any negative actions regarding student work" is guidance not to rest sanctions on detectors, P39. Instructor, when-misuse, "should be cautious" gives should-not.
units.anchor: Instructors should be cautious in relying on an AI detection tool
units.frag_end: conclusive evidence that they did not use AI.

units.why: "Training AI tools uses significant energy, raising concerns about sustainability" names an environmental cost, P53. A fact, so informs. Repeated in the staff section; coded once.
units.anchor: Training AI tools uses significant energy, raising concerns about sustainability.

units.why: "AI tools can produce incorrect or misleading information. Always fact-check the outputs." tells users to verify AI output, P31. "Always" makes it a must; student guide, during work.
units.anchor: Always fact-check the outputs.

units.why: "AI models may reflect biases in their training data" names bias as an ethical concern, P53. The "use critical thinking" part is a secondary verify instruction, but the unit mainly informs about bias.
units.anchor: AI models may reflect biases in their training data

units.why: "Avoid sharing sensitive or personal information with AI tools" protects personal data, P50. Student-addressed, during work, "Avoid" gives should-not. Repeated in the staff section; coded once.
units.anchor: Avoid sharing sensitive or personal information with AI tools

units.why: "SHSU has a contract with Copilot and Gemini to not use your information for training purposes" is a fact about vetted tools and data protection, P50. Informs.
units.anchor: SHSU has a contract with Copilot and Gemini
units.policy: SHSU has a contract with Copilot and Gemini under which the tools do not use student information for training purposes.

units.why: "While there is no defining university policy on AI, we continue to work together to integrate AI practice into existing and proposed policies" says SHSU has no AI policy of its own and folds AI into existing ones. P56 is a framework, P77 is about compliance; neither says this, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: there is no defining university policy on AI
units.uncovered_note: The university states it has no defining AI policy and is integrating AI into existing policies such as Academic Honesty and Course Structure and Management.

units.why: "living document ... lively, crowdsourced collection, inviting the contributions of stakeholders" says the guidance will evolve with contributions, P54. Admin, over-time, informs.
units.anchor: become a lively, crowdsourced collection, inviting the contributions of stakeholders

units.why: "The university has an emergent mandate from the state: integrate AI into classroom learning and student research projects" gives a workforce-readiness reason for AI in teaching, P44. Partial: it is a state mandate, not an employer-skill claim.
units.anchor: integrate AI into classroom learning and student research projects
units.fit_note: A state mandate to integrate AI into classes and student research for workforce readiness, not a course teaching AI as a skill.

units.why: "we remain true to our foundational commitment to guiding students through their intellectual development and acquisition of personal academic skills" balances AI integration against skill building, P41. Partial fit: it is a commitment, not a limit on AI.
units.anchor: foundational commitment to guiding students through their intellectual development
units.fit_note: A commitment to student skill acquisition stated as a counterweight to integrating AI; no limit on AI is stated.

units.why: "The purpose of this page is to provide resources for SHSU faculty and instructors seeking to create that balance" offers faculty resources, P63. Admin, before-course, informs.
units.anchor: provide resources for SHSU faculty and instructors seeking to create that balance

units.why: The page offers "examples of syllabus statements that cover different types of AI policies, ranging from a complete ban on AI tools to requiring the use of AI tools". It supports instructor choice of rule, so P04, partial because it supplies models rather than stating who decides.
units.anchor: syllabus statements that cover different types of AI policies
units.policy: The university offers examples of syllabus statements covering AI policies from a complete ban on AI tools to requiring AI tools for specific activities or assignments, many with rationale.
units.fit_note: Supplies sample syllabus statements across a ban-to-require range instead of stating who decides.

units.why: "educate them about the basics of how it actually works ... AI literacy" suggests instructors add introductory AI-literacy resources to courses. P70 (AI literacy for students) fits; "might add" gives may.
units.anchor: build a foundation of AI literacy
units.policy: Instructors might add resources to a course that educate students about how generative AI works, what it does well or poorly, and concerns with its use, to build a foundation of AI literacy.

units.why: "encourages employees to use institutionally approved AI tools, such as Microsoft Copilot and Google Gemini" prefers vetted tools for staff, P50. Staff, general; "encourages" so should.
units.anchor: encourages employees to use institutionally approved AI tools

units.why: "These platforms operate within university-supported security and privacy frameworks ... compliance with applicable regulations and policies, including FERPA, HIPAA" ties approved tools to legal compliance, P77. Informs.
units.anchor: including FERPA, HIPAA, and institutional data governance requirements

units.why: "should avoid entering sensitive, confidential, or protected data into non-approved AI applications" restricts data entry to unvetted tools, P50. Staff-addressed, "should avoid" gives should-not.
units.anchor: avoid entering sensitive, confidential, or protected data into non-approved AI applications

units.why: "Generative AI can help brainstorm ideas, summarize readings, draft outlines, sort data, and more" lists permitted staff uses. It is about administrative work, so P76 not P59 (teaching). May, permit.
units.anchor: Generative AI can help brainstorm ideas, summarize readings, draft outlines, sort data
units.fit_note: Lists permitted staff uses of AI (brainstorming, summarizing, outlines, sorting data) rather than rules for operations.

units.why: "Always verify AI-generated content for accuracy and originality" tells staff to verify AI output, P31. "Always" makes it must.
units.anchor: Always verify AI-generated content for accuracy and originality.

units.why: "Make sure to check with your supervisor before using an AI tool" requires staff to get supervisor clearance. P10 is about students asking instructors, so this is nearest to P76 (operational AI use) with a note.
units.anchor: Make sure to check with your supervisor before using an AI tool.
units.fit_note: Staff must clear AI tool use with a supervisor; the type covers operational rules but not this approval step.

units.why: "There are some tasks for which AI may not be appropriate, ethical, or even legal" warns staff that some AI uses are unlawful or improper, P77. Informs.
units.anchor: There are some tasks for which AI may not be appropriate, ethical, or even legal.
units.fit_note: Warns that some tasks are not appropriate, ethical or legal without naming the law or policy.

units.why: "Look into free tools like ChatGPT, DALL-E, or Grammarly’s AI writing assistant" recommends that staff try specific free tools. Nearest P76, but it is a tool suggestion rather than a rule; encourage.
units.anchor: Look into free tools like ChatGPT, DALL-E
units.fit_note: Suggests staff try free commercial AI tools; no operational rule.

units.why: "When writing an AI prompt, focus on persona, task, context and format." is advice on how to prompt. No type covers prompt-writing technique, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: When writing an AI prompt, focus on persona, task, context and format.
units.uncovered_note: Advice on how to write an effective prompt (persona, task, context, format).

units.why: "Run AI locally. Keep your data private. Maintain full control." recommends local LLMs for data privacy. P50 (protect data) is nearest; the advice to deploy local models is beyond the type, hence fit_note.
units.anchor: Run AI locally. Keep your data private.
units.fit_note: Recommends running local LLMs to keep data private, rather than using vetted institutional tools.

notes: Only one included document; no computing-unit or school policy. Repeated sentences (detector warning, academic-honesty sentence, environment/hallucination/privacy blocks in student and staff sections) coded once. Nav menus skipped.
